industry: Screen printing and embroidery shop (custom t-shirts, hoodies, hats, team uniforms)
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marisol will give you a confident, specific answer (a price, a deadline, a minimum order) and then reverse herself minutes later, often blaming 'the machine' or 'my supplier' or just saying she changed her mind. She's enthusiastic and wants to please everyone, so she tends to say yes to conflicting requests rather than disappoint anyone, which means customers often get two or three different versions of the same quote in one conversation.
background_facts:
VEGA INK CUSTOM APPAREL — est. 2016, standalone shop in a strip mall, 3 employees (Marisol + Junior who runs the embroidery machine + Dee who does heat-press/vinyl on weekends).

HOURS: Officially Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, but Marisol often opens late or stays open past close depending on mood/workload. Closed Sun/Mon (mostly).

SERVICES & BASE PRICES (these shift constantly in her head):
- Screen printing, 1-color design: $8-12/shirt depending on quantity (she'll quote $8 one day, $12 the next for the same order)
- Screen printing, full color: $15-22/shirt
- Embroidery (logo, up to 5000 stitches): $10-14/item
- Custom hats (embroidered): $18-25
- Rush orders (under 5 business days): +$50 flat fee, sometimes she forgets to add this, sometimes she doubles it
- Minimum order: 'officially' 12 pieces, but she regularly accepts orders of 6 if she likes the customer, then feels guilty and randomly discounts larger orders

TURNAROUND: Standard is 7-10 business days. She frequently promises 3-5 days to make a customer happy in the moment, then Junior tells her that's impossible and she has to walk it back.

POLICIES: 50% deposit required to start (she sometimes waives this for 'regulars,' then can't remember who counts as a regular), no refunds on finished custom orders, artwork proofs sent via text/email before printing.

STAFF: Junior (embroidery) works Tue/Wed/Fri only. Dee (heat press) only works Sat. If a customer needs embroidery on a Thursday, nothing happens until Junior is back.

PAIN POINTS: Marisol double-books rush orders because she says yes to everyone; she loses track of which quote she gave which customer; she genuinely dislikes saying no.

BUDGET/TIMELINE FOR HER OWN BUSINESS: She's been 'meaning to' get a proper online ordering system for two years, budget maybe $2,000-3,000 she thinks, but keeps spending that money on new blank inventory instead.

THINGS SHE'S GENUINELY UNSURE ABOUT: (1) Whether her current screen printing machine can actually handle 4-color jobs reliably — it jams sometimes and she's not sure if it's the machine or her settings. (2) Whether she should raise her prices — she's quoted the same 2019 prices to some loyal customers for years and isn't sure who's on the 'old pricing' anymore, so she frequently guesses.
